# Review checklist

Tick each item or write why it does not apply.

## Facts
- [ ] Every history claim has a fact-sheet id with a URL and a check date.
- [ ] No [S], [C] or [GAP] claim is stated as a plain fact.
- [ ] Every game claim matches the recorded build or is labelled "in development".
- [ ] Every quote has a row on the quote sheet, with the full sentence for an excerpt.
- [ ] Translated quotes name the translator or institution and year in captions and source notes; cards carry no translator line. Missing details remain gaps.
- [ ] Official translation excerpts are labelled as such; retained wording differences have a linked owner decision.
- [ ] No quote is invented, merged or shortened to change its meaning.
- [ ] No private thought or feeling is attributed to a real person.

## Voice
- [ ] A cold viewer can follow every line: places, groups and terms are named at first mention, and the plain fact comes before any image or contrast line.
- [ ] Every voice-over line teaches something: a date, a number, a place, a name or a consequence.
- [ ] There is a story: a viewer can retell it in two sentences (who, what problem, what was decided, what it cost).
- [ ] Picture and voice tell the same story. A decision card on screen is the decision the voice describes.
- [ ] No unexplained gap over five seconds, and no empty cue.
- [ ] It sounds like a briefing, not a trailer. No phrase from the "fails review" list.
- [ ] One idea per spoken sentence. No sentence over 18 words without a reason.
- [ ] No verdict words (brave, tragic, miraculous). The fact carries the weight.
- [ ] Person and tense are consistent (you, now; they, then).
- [ ] No dashes in written text.

## Framing and sensitivity
- [ ] The Israeli framing is stated, not softened and not turned into a slogan.
- [ ] War, terror and the Holocaust are handled through facts and archival material only.
- [ ] No imagery of the camps, no Nazi symbols, no video for a Deport option.
- [ ] A sensitive event is flagged for owner review.

## Honesty about what is shown
- [ ] Real build footage names the build and commit.
- [ ] Concept art and AI footage are labelled as such, on screen.
- [ ] No gameplay is implied that is not in the build.
- [ ] The call to action refers to something that exists today.
- [ ] No placeholder art, debug text or unfinished UI is visible in any frame.
- [ ] The labels on screen match the recorded build, and the build id is recorded.

## Sound and access
- [ ] The key message survives with the sound off.
- [ ] Every voice-over and on-screen word is in the captions, in English and Hebrew.
- [ ] Synthetic voice or music is disclosed in the description and in `ASSETS.yaml`, and the README and Steam text are in step.
- [ ] No synthetic voice speaks as a real person.
- [ ] Pronunciation matches the signed-off list.

## Hebrew
- [ ] Written natively, not translated line by line.
- [ ] A named native reader signed off the captions and any Hebrew voice, with a date.

## Records
- [ ] Script, fact sheet, quote sheet, voice brief and build id are stored with the cut.
